outcome.text: {"perspective":"software","title":"Conditional local checker for synthetic grid edge mismatches","mechanism":"C1 identifies adjacent-edge mismatches as the target. A proposed deterministic checker would enumerate each internal adjacency once, compare the two facing edge symbols under an agreed matching rule, and report tile coordinates, edge directions and observed symbols for each mismatch. It would distinguish invalid or missing data from genuine mismatches rather than silently treating them as matches. C2 supports plausibility, not demonstrated superiority: the inspected viewer lacks this check, but manual checking and other tools have not been compared.","intended_users":"Simulated tile-pattern exercise participants reviewing the single approved synthetic grid file; no real-user or deployment scope.","smallest_version":"Specify a read-only local script for one agreed file format, without a UI, network access or file modification. For a rectangular grid, compare each tile's right edge with its right neighbor's left edge and its bottom edge with the next row's top edge. Report mismatches in a plain-text list and report parsing failures separately. Before implementation, obtain the approved file/schema and agreement on equality versus complementary-symbol rules, orientation, missing cells and boundary behavior. Limit any later trial to the approved synthetic file and explicitly authorized test cases. No implementation or execution is claimed here.","measurable_outcome":"Propose comparing checker flags with a manually adjudicated list for the approved grid: missed mismatches, false flags and review time, including setup time. No comparison has run and no benefit is established.","feasibility":"For an agreed rectangular representation and constant-time edge rule, one pass over internal adjacencies is technically straightforward. However, the packet supplies neither file contents nor a schema or agreed rules, so a runnable implementation cannot be specified reliably. C2 leaves comparative value unresolved. Defer building until those inputs and a bounded comparison are authorized; use manual review if setup would exceed the effort of checking this single grid. Evidence is synthetic only and does not establish transferability.","maintenance":"Keep scope to one format and rule version. Any later format or matching-rule change requires revalidation; avoid a service, integrations or ongoing deployment for this one-file exercise.","software_warranted":{"verdict":"unclear","reason":"The viewer's missing adjacency check (C2) suggests a possible gap, but does not justify new software by itself. For one grid, manual review or an existing local tool may be cheaper than script setup and validation. Human judgment is needed to settle edge semantics and adjudicate a reference list. Consider a custom checker only if the approved format and rules make it small and a bounded comparison indicates worthwhile error reduction or total effort savings; neither has been established."},"recommendation":"consider","claim_refs":["C1","C2"],"assumptions":[{"statement":"Facing-edge compatibility can be expressed as a deterministic rule agreed by the exercise owner.","would_change":"If compatibility depends on interpretation, retain human review rather than automatically labeling mismatches."},{"statement":"The approved file contains explicit tile positions and edge symbols in a locally readable format.","would_change":"If extraction or conversion is substantial, prefer manual checking or an existing viewer/export workflow before custom development."},{"statement":"The exercise uses rectangular adjacency without implicit rotation or wrapping; this is a proposed scope, not an observed fact.","would_change":"If topology, orientation or boundaries differ, revise the specification before implementation."},{"statement":"Only one synthetic grid needs checking, and comparative effort is unknown.","would_change":"A very small grid favors manual review; documented repeated checking needs or a favorable bounded comparison could justify a minimal custom checker."}],"novelty":null,"response_to_findings":null}

{"perspective":"process_change","title":"Check seed-type annotation before sealing; hold incomplete envelopes","mechanism":"C1 identifies a sequencing failure: envelopes are sealed before annotation presence is checked. Use the agreed paper sequence in C2 as a pre-sealing gate: inspect the annotation, seal only if present, and place incomplete envelopes in a clearly marked hold area. A simulated desk participant resolves missing information rather than guessing the seed type. This targets annotation presence, not botanical correctness; C2 leaves both correctness and adherence untested.","intended_users":"Simulated seed-library desk participants handling returned seed envelopes; no real users or deployment are included.","smallest_version":"Propose a paper instruction beside the sealing station: check annotation, hold if missing, seal if present. Mark separate ready-to-seal and held areas. For a bounded simulation, compare 20 mock returns under the described seal-first sequence with 20 matched mock returns under the check-first sequence, using the same distribution of initially missing annotations. Record annotation presence at sealing, held items, skipped checks and handling time. Use a supplied mock answer key, if available, to assess correctness separately. This is a proposed comparison only; no trial or approval is claimed.","measurable_outcome":"Compare the proportion sealed without annotations, skipped-check rate, unresolved held items and handling time across the two sequences. Assess annotation correctness separately only with a mock answer key; no achieved improvement is claimed.","feasibility":"C2 supplies an agreed paper sequence and states that no integration is needed. The proposed hold rule extends that sequence without new software or spending. A comparison needs mock envelopes, initial annotation states and a tally sheet; correctness assessment additionally needs known mock seed types. Only C1 and C2 are available synthetic observations, so real-world feasibility, adherence and benefit remain unvalidated. No comparison was executed in this assignment.","maintenance":"Keep the paper instruction and hold area visible; review skipped checks and unresolved holds after each simulated batch. Revise the sequence if holding becomes a backlog or participants bypass the check.","software_warranted":{"verdict":"no","reason":"The supplied mechanism is an ordering error, and C2 already provides a paper check-before-seal sequence with no integration need. A paper gate and human handling of exceptions address it directly. Existing digital tools would be optional tally aids, not a prerequisite; custom software would add maintenance without evidence of a gap. Reconsider only if a bounded comparison exposes persistent failures that simpler workflow changes cannot resolve."},"recommendation":"recommend","claim_refs":["C1","C2"],"assumptions":[{"statement":"Participants can leave incomplete envelopes unsealed in a distinct hold area within the simulation.","would_change":"If envelopes must be sealed immediately or cannot be held safely, move the annotation check earlier in intake rather than adopt this hold rule."},{"statement":"The immediate goal is annotation presence; a written seed type is not necessarily correct.","would_change":"If correctness is required, add a separate verification procedure using reliable identification evidence; do not treat presence as success on correctness."},{"statement":"The agreed paper sequence can be followed, but adherence and exception resolution remain untested.","would_change":"If checks are bypassed or held items accumulate, revise station layout and responsibility before considering automation."}],"novelty":null,"response_to_findings":null}
